reasons: Classification is correct: p0042 imposes a mutual consent requirement on every assignment with no successor or affiliate carve-out, so it fails the fallback ('mutual right to assign to successors with written notice'), even though the reasonableness qualifier keeps it out of walk-away territory.

Redline is valid and directionally right for the customer: it preserves the existing mutual reasonable-consent standard and merely appends the affiliate/successor carve-out for Company plus the no-assignment-to-competitor limit on Contractor, both drawn from the preferred position.

The failed 'minimal edit' check is an artefact of appending a proviso to a short clause — no original language was deleted or weakened, so the edit is substantively the smallest change that reaches the playbook position.
Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice, explains the change, cites the playbook basis and offers the successor-on-notice fallback.
Rationale correctly confirms no change-of-control trigger exists in the Agreement, so no deletion is required for that element; no double-flagging of the same term.
